content.title: What is the Executor Framework?
content.description: The Executor Framework is a high-level concurrency framework in Java that simplifies thread management by separating task submission from thread creation and execution.

content.content: Creating and managing threads manually becomes difficult as applications grow. The Executor Framework, introduced in Java 5 under the java.util.concurrent package, provides thread pools, task scheduling, and efficient resource management. Developers submit tasks to an executor, which handles thread creation, reuse, and scheduling automatically.

content.title: Why Use the Executor Framework?
content.content: It improves application performance by reusing threads, reducing thread creation overhead, simplifying concurrency, and providing scalable task execution.
The Executor Framework consists of several important interfaces and classes that work together to manage concurrent task execution efficiently.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Instead of creating threads manually, submit tasks to an ExecutorService and let the framework manage execution.

content.content: ExecutorService is the most commonly used interface. It provides methods to submit tasks, manage thread pools, and shut down executors safely.

items.question: Fixed Thread Pool
items.answer: Creates a fixed number of reusable threads.

items.question: Cached Thread Pool
items.answer: Creates new threads as needed and reuses idle threads.

items.question: Single Thread Executor
items.answer: Executes tasks sequentially using a single worker thread.

items.question: Scheduled Thread Pool
items.answer: Schedules tasks to execute after delays or periodically.

content.title: Where is the Executor Framework Used?

items.question: Web Servers
items.answer: Handle thousands of client requests efficiently using thread pools.

items.question: Background Processing
items.answer: Execute long-running tasks without blocking the main application.

items.question: Scheduled Jobs
items.answer: Run periodic maintenance, backups, and monitoring tasks.

content.title: Restaurant Staff
content.content: Instead of hiring a new waiter for every customer, a restaurant keeps a team of waiters ready to serve incoming customers. Similarly, a thread pool reuses existing threads instead of creating new ones for every task.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: ExecutorService, thread pools, Callable, Runnable, Future, ScheduledExecutorService, shutdown(), submit(), execute(), and ForkJoinPool are common Java concurrency interview topics.

items.question: Should shutdown() be ignored?
items.answer: No. Always shut down an ExecutorService to release system resources.

items.question: Can Runnable return a value?
items.answer: No. Use Callable when a result is required.

items.question: Should a new thread pool be created for every task?
items.answer: No. Reuse thread pools whenever possible to improve performance.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: The Executor Framework simplifies concurrent programming by managing reusable thread pools and separating task execution from thread management.
